  FOR SPECIAL MEETING

  CITY COUNCIL

ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.

  NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Mayor of the City of Norwalk has called a special meeting of the City
Council beginning at 5:00 p.m. on May 25, 2021 via video conference. The agenda for the special meeting is as
follows:

CALL TO ORDER  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL  City Clerk

REPORT

FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 PROPOSED BUDGET - The Fiscal Year 2021/22 Proposed Budget is presented for
discussion and direction.

I, Theresa Devoy, City Clerk, hereby certify that the foregoing notice of special meeting was posted at City Hall not less than 24-
hours before the start of the meeting and delivered to each member of the Norwalk City Council and to the following newspapers:
Herald American, Cerritos Community News, Norwalk Patriot, and Whittier Daily News, all on the 21st day of May 2021.

Theresa Devoy, CMC, City Clerk

  Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
  posted will also be made available for public inspection in the City Clerk’s Department.

  Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the City Council on any matter listed on the agenda.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s office, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet, can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 12 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.
   City Council Agenda Report
  May 25, 2021

TO:  Honorable City Council

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager

BY:  Jana Stuard, Director of Finance /Treasurer

SUBJECT: FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 PROPOSED BUDGET

Background:

Each year the City is required by the Norwalk Municipal Code to prepare an annual budget
and present it to City Council for public consideration. The proposed budget for the
upcoming fiscal year, which covers the period July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022, was
presented to the Finance Ad Hoc Committee on May 7, 2021 and distributed to the
members of City Council on May 19. The document was also made available for public
review in the City Clerk’s Department and on the City’s web page.

The Fiscal Year (FY) 2021/22 Proposed Budget contains the following sections:
  Ø Summaries:
  ü Changes to Fund Balances/Working Capital
  ü Inter-Fund Transfers
  ü All Funds – Expenditure Summary
  ü All Funds – Full Time and Part Time Hours
  ü General Fund Revenue Summary
  ü General Fund Expenditure Summaries by Type and Function
  Ø Revenues – all funds
  Ø Capital Outlays
  Ø Capital Projects – carryover and new projects.
  Ø Departmental Detail – contains the following information for each departmental
  division (Budget Unit):
  ü Activities and Objectives
  ü Personnel Information – summarizes budgeted full-time positions and part-
  time hours.
  ü Activity Detail – contains the explanation and/or the breakdown of certain
  expenditure line items, such as: contract services, membership, special
  studies, special projects, etc.
  ü Departmental Expenditure Budget – details line items per Budget Unit.
 City Council  May 25, 2021
Fiscal Year 2021/22 Proposed Budget  Page No. 2

The financial plan assumes that the City will resume its normal operations at the pre-
COVID-19 levels. The FY 2021/22 Budget is balanced by using the City’s available
resources, including the newly voter-approved 0.75% additional local sales tax, to fund
primarily public safety enhancements for both the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
Department and City’s community policing services, as well as other operating
expenditures. The available General Fund balance is used to replenish the City’s capital
reserves, primarily the Street Renovation Fund.

Subsequent to City Council direction at this and following budget review meetings, a final
budget will be prepared and submitted for adoption at a public hearing scheduled for a
meeting in June.

In addition, as part of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (ARPA), the U.S.
Department of the Treasury (the Treasury) established the Coronavirus State and Local
Fiscal Recovery Funds of $350 billion, out of which the City will receive a little over $28
million. Spending of the ARPA resources is not part of the Proposed Budget document,
as the Treasury published the spending guidelines only on May 10, 2021, and staff needs
additional time to prepare the City’s spending plan for City Council’s consideration and
approval.

Fiscal Impact:

Contingent on City Council’s direction, the proposed budget, when adopted, will serve as
the City’s expenditure plan for a one-year period, covering July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022.

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Plan 2021 Implementation:

The recommended action adhers to the City’s values to be fiscally responsible, ethical
and transparent in City’s stewardship; and it will further the City’s strategic plan goal (3)
Maintain strong local tax base to support City operations.

Recommended Action:

The Fiscal Year 2021/22 Proposed Budget is presented for discussion and direction.
